chunks: Ibn Mahbub narrated from Nuʿaym ibn Ibrahim, from Mismāʿ Abī Sayyār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
"The offense of an umm al-walad regarding the rights of people is upon her master."
He said: "And whatever pertains to the right of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, that is upon her body."
He said: "Retaliation is taken from her for the slaves, and there is no qisas between the free person and the slave."

key_terms.أُمُّ ٱلْوَلَدِ: A slave woman who has borne a child to her master
key_terms.بَدَنِهَا: Her body; meaning the punishment is carried out upon her person
key_terms.حَقِّ ٱللَّهِ: The right of Allah, meaning offenses classified as divine rights
key_terms.حُقُوقِ ٱلنَّاسِ: The rights owed to other people
key_terms.يُقَاصُّ: Retaliation is exacted or legal retribution is taken

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the offense of an umm al-walad in the rights of people and the right of Allah?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about the liability of an umm al-walad. It distinguishes between violations involving the rights of people, for which her master bears responsibility, and violations involving the right of Allah, which are carried out upon her own person. It also states that qisas may be enforced in relation to slaves, while there is no qisas between a free person and a slave.
